title: Diagnosing the Unknown for Care and Advancing Science (DUCAS)
text:
Without access to an integrated approach to diagnosis, research, and care, many patients with rare conditions
go from one institution to the next without finding answers or making progress with their care. This leads to
poor outcomes for patients and families and poses a burden on our healthcare system. As part of this project,
we will create sustainable, national infrastructure to address this unmet need for those who are undiagnosed.

title: Computational, Neural, and Behavioral Studies of Competition-Dependent Learning
text:
Our ability to distinguish similar perceptual inputs is crucial for everyday functioning (e.g., what information to
share with which person, which objects are safe to eat); failing to make such distinctions can lead to mundane
errors and memory interference, but also to devastating cognitive, semantic, communication, and developmental
deficits. This combined computational and experimental project proposes and tests a new theory of how two key
brain structures — the hippocampus and visual cortex — collaborate to support learning of distinctions through
a process of differentiation. The resulting knowledge will advance our fundamental understanding of memory in
the human brain and guide the creation of evidence-based training curricula for learning to distinguish people,
places, and things that otherwise risk being confused, with potential applications to new interventions for psychi-
atric and neurological disorders.

title: Normalizing PDAC stroma with PCBP2 siRNA nanoparticles to improve the antitumor activity of chemotherapy and immunotherapy
text:
Dense desmoplastic stroma is a fundamental characteristic of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma
(PDAC) and comprises up to 80% of the tumor mass. While the strategy to deplete PDAC stroma has
failed in clinical trials, normalization of the stroma to allow chemotherapy to kill the tumor cells in the
“nest” could be a promising strategy for PDAC therapy. In this proposal, we will evaluate how the
PCBP2 siRNA enhances the anti-tumor activity of chemotherapy and immunotherapy for PDAC.

title: Hepatocellular determinants of lipid storage and secretion
text:
Abnormal accumulation of neutral lipids in liver hepatocytes is a defining feature of metabolic dysfunction-
associated fatty liver disease (MAFLD), a widespread condition that can progress to cirrhosis and liver failure.
The molecular pathways that determine whether lipids are stored in lipid droplets or secreted as lipoproteins
remain poorly understood. This research will uncover key mechanisms that govern lipid partitioning in
hepatocytes, offering potential targets for new therapies to prevent or treat fatty liver disease.

title: Deep Learning Based Natural Language Processing Markers of Anxiety and Depression
text:
The efficient assessment of Major Depressive Disorder (MDD) and Generalized Anxiety Disorder (GAD) is a
significant impending public health challenge. The proposed project aims to study digital biomarkers from large
language models as a novel methodology and to apply them to quantify MDD and GAD symptoms. The project
aims to increase our understanding of depression and anxiety by examining and preliminarily validating
computational linguistic features, and will result in an improved empirical framework and associated digital
tools to move psychiatric assessment of MDD and GAD from subjective ratings.

title: Pilot Project 1:  Creating Bridges to Reproductive Health Care for Rural Adolescent and Young Adult Cancer Survivors
text: PROJECT SUMMARY/ ABSTRACT – PILOT PROJECT Reproductive health care in cancer patients is an unmet need in Imperial County, a medically underserved, rural region of the Cancer Research and Education to Advance HealTh Equity (CREATE) Partnership’s catchment area with a predominantly Hispanic population. Reproductive health is a major issue for adolescent and young adult (AYA) cancer survivors because they can experience higher risks of infertility, adverse pregnancy outcomes, and unmet informational needs. Reproductive health care effectively reduces risks, but uptake is low because there are no scalable interventions to support the implementation of routine reproductive health care in underserved, geographically remote communities. Guided by the Cancer Survivorship Care Quality Framework, this pilot proposal seeks to adapt and pilot test a multi-component intervention to improve reproductive health care uptake by female AYA cancer survivors. The intervention has three components derived from our prior work: 1) a reproductive risk summary (RS) and survivorship care plan on reproductive health (SCP-R), 2) navigation, and 3) telehealth reproductive consults. In Aim 1, we will adapt the RS and SCP-R in English and Spanish to be responsive to the cultural, health literacy, and socio-ecological needs of Latina AYA survivors through focus groups with AYA survivors and parents/guardians, and semi-structured interviews with healthcare providers. We will also systematically evaluate barriers and facilitators to reproductive health care in Imperial County and examine how to fit the multi-component intervention to this setting, through focus groups with survivors and parents/guardians and interviews with healthcare providers and clinic staff. In Aim 2, we will conduct feasibility testing of the multicomponent intervention in a single arm pilot hybrid type 1 trial (evaluating effectiveness and observing implementation). The primary outcome is engagement in reproductive health care by 15 newly diagnosed and 15 post-treatment AYA survivors. Secondarily, we will qualitatively assess effectiveness, fit and implementation outcomes with AYA survivors, healthcare providers and health clinic staff. The proposal directly targets a critical health disparity faced by female AYA survivors in our catchment area and need for partnership between rural community health professionals and urban specialists to deliver quality reproductive survivorship care. We will generate a novel, scalable intervention and preliminary data to support a future multi-site trial on intervention effectiveness in increasing reproductive care in rural, medically underserved oncology settings. The partnership between SDSU, CRCD and UCSD researchers will be strengthened with collaborative learning, community engagement, and increased capacity of trainees to support future cancer research in Imperial County.

title: Aging and Rejuvenation of Skin Stem Cells
text:
With age, the body’s ability to repair and regenerate tissues gradually decline. Using hair follicle stem cells
(HFSCs) as a model for studying stem cell changes during aging, we will identify genes that can functionally
rejuvenate old HFSCs or drive HFSC aging. These results are not only important for the mechanistic
understanding of HFSC aging, but may also inform innovative therapeutic solutions to halt or revert age-related
decline seen with stem cells.

title: Determining the Role of Mitochondrial Hydrogen Peroxide in the Regulation of Neuronal Mitochondrial Networks
text:
Impaired mitochondrial function is associated with the onset and progression of neurodegenerative
disease. Mitochondrial remodeling processes – fission and fusion – combat mitochondrial functional decline,
but their regulatory mechanisms are incompletely understood. In this proposal, we aim to determine if
mitochondrial hydrogen peroxide (mtH2O2) regulates neuronal mitochondrial fission and fusion via local
oxidation events and if these processes occur differently across neuronal compartments.

title: Balancing dysplastic repair versus regeneration in the lung
text:
Lung injury can lead to improper repair, contributing to chronic diseases like emphysema and fibrosis. Basal
stem cells invade the alveolar niche after injury, disrupting normal repair and inhibiting AT2 cell regeneration.
Our research explores how Notch and Wnt signaling regulate this injury-induced tissue niche (iTCH) and its role
in dysplastic versus euplastic repair, with potential implications for diagnosing and treating lung diseases.

title: Metastable Crystallins: Structure and Stabilization
text:
Understanding how eye lens crystallins can be activated and whether the activated crystallins
have better cellular protection capacity will help future studies of identifying most active form of
crystallins to treat disease conditions. The proposed study will include studies on the changes
occurring in crystallin protein molecule during activation and testing the active preparations in
cell culture models replicating stress conditions.

title: Development of an early tooth organoid via human induced pluripotent stem cells
text:
This proposal aims to derive the earliest dental progenitors, i.e. the cells that can develop to form a whole,
functional tooth, from human induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs). The robust derivation of such progenitors
with robust odontogenic (dentin and enamel) potential will set the foundation for the establishment of an iPSC-
derived human tooth germ to be used for research/clinical ends. Applications range from development of in vitro
models of tooth development, to “disease-in-a-dish” modeling of and development of therapies for congenital
dental defects.

title: Altered RNA fates due to an MDS driver mutation in SF3B1
text:
Mutations in proteins that process ribonucleic acids (RNA) are highly prevalent in myelodysplastic syndromes
(MDS), a chronic blood disorder that causes anemia, bleeding and risk of transforming to leukemia. This proposal
seeks to understand basic mechanisms by which these mutant proteins dysregulate cellular function. This will
help us develop better targeted therapies for these disorders.

title: The role of lung capillary endothelial cells in NFkB-directed alveolarization
text:
Nearly half of preterm infants develop bronchopulmonary dysplasia (BPD). Chronic lung diseases, like BPD,
resulting from irreversible pathological changes to vasculature-epithelial interactions are top causes of death,
without adequate therapies to reverse changes and reduce morbidity/mortality. Completion of this proposed
research will elucidate molecular mechanisms governing developmental vascular-epithelial interactions to
illuminate putative therapeutic targets that can reduce morbidity/mortality in chronic lung diseases like BPD.

title: Development of dual inhibitors targeting the viral main protease and the host cathepsin L as SARS-CoV-2 antivirals
text:
Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) is a viral pathogen that leads to the
COVID-19 pandemic. Currently there is no approved antiviral drug or vaccine for the respiratory diseases
associated with SARS-CoV-2 infection. To address the unmet medical need, we will develop potent and
selective SARS-CoV-2 inhibitors with high potency and selectivity, broad-spectrum antiviral activity, and
favorable pharmacokinetic properties by targeting the viral main protease and the host cathepsin L, and
provide lead candidates for the in vivo animal model studies.

title: Ultrafast Dynamic contract optical coherence tomography for high-throughput anti-cancer drug screening
text: Improving the success rate of oncology drug development requires pre ... clinical models that better mimic in vivo tumor environments and advanced imaging tools capable of real-time monitoring of treatment responses. Tumor organoids represent a biologically relevant 3D cancer model, yet existing imaging platforms fall short in achieving both high temporal resolution and high throughput. To address this critical gap, we propose to develop an ultrafast Dynamic Contrast Optical Coherence Tomography (DyC-OCT) system empowered by artificial intelligence (Al) for label-free, high-throughput 4D imaging of tumor organoids.

title: A Platform for Arene Activation via Machine Learning and Small Molecule Catalysis
text:
Synthetic methods for the late-stage modification of pharmaceutical compounds have the potential to
rapidly expand the ability for medicinal chemists to synthesize and test new lead drug compounds. Furthermore,
arene rings are exceptionally prevalent in pharmaceutical compounds. The following proposal details a method
for the activation and functionalization of arene rings through arene epoxidation to allow for a variety of diverse
and valuable products to be synthesized, and this proposal will be achieved via machine learning catalyst
optimization and hit development.

title: A Dose Expansion Study of SX-682 Alone and in Combination with Decitabine in MDS Patients
text:
Myelodysplastic syndromes (MDS) is a pre-leukemic syndrome to acute myeloid leukemia (AML), with treatment
options limited to only 4 drugs with regulatory approval for MDS, including azacitidine and decitabine. Once
these agents fail in patients (typically in 1-2 years), there is no second-line treatment, resulting in dismal
prognoses: <6 months for higher-risk patients, and <18 months for lower-risk patients. This proposal is a clinical
trial wherein the novel, immunotherapeutic drug SX-682 is evaluated in combination with decitabine, which if
successful, would dramatically transform the treatment landscape for MDS.

title: Mechanisms of Cellular Communication: The Role of Merlin in Pancreatic Development
text:
Progenitor, or stem cells, that give rise to insulin-producing islet cells emerge from embryonic endodermal
epithelium within the early pancreatic bud. This work focuses on the basic molecular mechanisms that shape
the cellular microenvironment and 3D epithelial architecture where pancreatic endocrine cells are born.
Understanding these basic processes will lead to novel insights into regenerative and replacement therapies
for diabetes mellitus.

title: Project 2: Rational approaches to improve treatment outcomes of patients with breast cancer brain metastases
text:
The development of effective therapies for patients with breast cancer brain metastases remains a critical unmet
medical need. Our preliminary data from preclinical and clinical studies suggest a role for antibody drug
conjugates (ADC) in monotherapy and combination approaches to treat patients with brain metastases and
suggest rational strategies to augment ADC activity by increasing payload expression and by targeting PI3Kβ to
enhance anti-tumor immunity. Our overarching goals are to develop rational and effective strategies to
dramatically improve outcomes in patients with this devastating site of cancer metastasis, not only in breast
cancer, but potentially across multiple solid tumors.

title: AI-Powered MRI Quality Control and Artifact Correction for Multi-Site Studies
text:
This project will equip neuroscience researchers, radiologists, MRI technologists, and study coordinators with au-
tomatic, objective, fast, and accurate tools for image quality assessment so that timely decisions for re-scans can
be made to improve the likelihood of collecting usable structural MRI data of sufficient sample size for subsequent
analyses. Our tools will allow (i) high-speed image quality assessment with high specificity and sensitivity, (ii) ret-
rospective artifact correction without the need for modification of pulse sequences or mounting of motion markers,
and (iii) method generalizability and optimality for multiple sites, scanners, and imaging protocols without explicit
data sharing. Successful completion of this project will allow image quality assurance to be done automatically in
large-scale, multi-site, and longitudinal studies, and increase the amount of usable data for improving statistical
power.
